findings.title: Analytics event recorded before feature-flag and input validation checks
findings.body: In `ProjectPreprodArtifactAssembleEndpoint.post`, `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` is called unconditionally at the very top of the handler, before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble", ...)` check and before the request body is validated. As a result, an analytics event is recorded for every POST to this endpoint even when the organization does not have the feature enabled (which returns a 404) or when the payload is malformed (which returns a 400). This pollutes the `preprod_artifact.api.assemble` analytics stream with events for requests that never actually assembled anything, making the metric unreliable for its intended purpose. The call should be moved after the feature check (and ideally after successful validation).

findings.title: Static method on CommitContextIntegration references unrelated class PRCommentWorkflow
findings.body: The new staticmethod `CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)` instead of `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title(title)` (or just calling the sibling staticmethod directly), even though `_truncate_title` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration` itself a few lines above. This only works if `PRCommentWorkflow` happens to inherit from `CommitContextIntegration`; if that class hierarchy changes, or if this method is ever reused from a context where `PRCommentWorkflow` is not in scope/does not inherit the helper, this will raise an AttributeError. Referencing a specific subclass by name from a base-class method is a fragile and confusing design that should instead reference the class that actually owns the method.

findings.title: Exception object passed directly into logger extra, failure silently swallowed at info level
findings.body: In `CommitContextIntegration.get_environment_info`, the except block logs `extra={"issue_id": issue.id, "error": e}` where `e` is the raw exception instance rather than `str(e)`. Passing non-serializable objects (like exceptions) into logging `extra` can break log processors/formatters that try to JSON-serialize log records (e.g. structured logging pipelines), and since this is logged at `logger.info` level with a broad `except Exception`, any real bug in `get_recommended_event()`/`get_environment()` (e.g., a programming error, not just "no environment") will be silently absorbed without being captured by Sentry or surfaced at a visible log level.

findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization wired with hardcoded empty data instead of actual query results
findings.body: In `WidgetCardChart.tableResultComponent`, when `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, the new `<TableWidgetVisualization>` component is rendered with `columns={[]}` and `tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}` — completely hardcoded empty values — instead of being derived from `result`/`fields`/`eventView` like the `StyledSimpleTableChart` branch it replaces. Any organization with this feature flag enabled will see a permanently blank table widget regardless of the actual query results, since none of the real `tableResults` data is passed through.

findings.title: fetch_error_details misaligns error ids with event data when ids repeat or are missing
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids` (which may contain duplicates, e.g. if the same error occurred multiple times in a replay) and fetches them via `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)`, then zips `error_ids` with `events.values()`. Because dict keys must be unique, duplicate node ids collapse into a single entry in the `events` dict, making `events.values()` shorter than `error_ids`. `zip()` silently truncates to the shorter sequence, so after the first duplicate (or any backend behavior that omits missing keys rather than returning them with `None`), every subsequent `(event_id, data)` pair is shifted and misattributed to the wrong `error_id`, producing incorrect titles/timestamps/messages in the generated AI summary log. A safer implementation would look up each entry explicitly via `events.get(node_id)` keyed by the corresponding node id rather than relying on positional correspondence between two independently constructed sequences.

findings.title: No test coverage for duplicate or missing error ids in fetch_error_details/get_request_data
findings.body: The new tests (test_get_with_error, test_get_with_error_context_disabled, test_get_request_data) only cover the straightforward case of a single, successfully-found error event. There is no test exercising `fetch_error_details` with duplicate `error_ids` or with an `error_id` that is absent from nodestore, which is exactly the scenario where the `zip(error_ids, events.values())` pairing in `fetch_error_details` can misattribute error data to the wrong id (see related finding on project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py).

findings.title: Environment filter silently dropped when fetching trace item attribute keys
findings.body: The previous implementation in useTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx sent `environment: selection.environments` as part of the query to the trace-items attributes endpoint. The new shared `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` helper omits this parameter entirely, with only a comment stating '// environment left out intentionally as it's not supported'. This removes previously-existing environment-scoped filtering of attribute/tag keys without any test asserting the new (or old) behavior, so if the backend does support environment filtering, this is a silent regression that will surface irrelevant attribute keys from other environments in the Explore UI.
